title: Illumination of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Illumination of Scripture is the work of the Holy Spirit by which He helps believers understand, receive, and apply God’s Word. Illumination does not add new Scripture; it enables God’s people to see and respond rightly to what God has already spoken.
summary: Illumination of Scripture is the work of the Holy Spirit by which He helps believers understand, receive, and apply God’s Word. Illumination does not add new Scripture; it enables God’s people to see and respond rightly to what God has already spoken.
christFocus: The Spirit opens hearts to behold the truth of Christ in Scripture. Through illumination, believers see more clearly the glory, grace, authority, sufficiency, and saving work of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s Word is true and clear, but fallen people need divine help to receive it rightly. Sin blinds the heart, resists correction, twists truth, and prefers darkness. Illumination is God’s gracious work of opening understanding.

Illumination does not mean every believer instantly understands every passage without study. It does not replace reading, context, teaching, prayer, or careful interpretation. Rather, the Spirit works through these means to give spiritual understanding and faithful response.

Jesus opened the minds of His disciples to understand the Scriptures. The same need remains for believers today. Understanding Scripture is not merely an academic task; it is a spiritual work that calls for humility and dependence.

The Spirit shines light into the heart so believers can recognize truth, treasure Christ, repent of sin, trust God’s promises, and walk in obedience. Illumination is not given to make people proud, but to make them faithful.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A person can read the Bible and still resist what God is saying. Scripture can be studied for arguments, information, control, or pride while the heart remains unchanged. People need more than open eyes on a page; they need opened hearts before God.

This doctrine gives hope to ordinary believers. God is willing to help His people understand His Word. The confused, new, weak, wounded, and untrained are invited to pray, “Open my eyes,” trusting that the Spirit gives light.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to open your eyes when you read Scripture. Come humbly, not as one trying to control the Word, but as one needing to be taught. Study carefully, receive faithful teaching, and depend on the Spirit to help you understand, believe, repent, obey, and see Christ more clearly.
